## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `85ef16b866860b12de8afe3ed21a5de5979fb6f7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: every path of the diff outside the changeset (40 paths: `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts`, `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/sharedDiscovery.ts`, the 28 in-package test files, the 4 console, 4 app-shell and 2 react test files) + read to judge it: `.changeset/25921-data-objectstack-shared-discovery-cache-helper.md`, `ui/packages/data-objectstack/package.json`, `ui/packages/data-objectstack/tsup.config.ts`, `ui/packages/data-objectstack/tsconfig.json`, `ui/packages/data-objectstack/README.md`, `ui/vitest.config.mts`, `ui/apps/console/vitest.config.ts`, `ui/apps/console/vite.config.ts`, `ui/apps/console/src/languageSeed.ts`, `ui/packages/app-shell/src/chrome/ConditionalAuthWrapper.tsx`, `ui/packages/app-shell/package.json`, `ui/packages/react/tsconfig.test.json`, `scripts/check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs`, `AGENTS.md` (changeset rule), `main` at `e9884e19`, and the org-wide code search for the retired name

### ① Derived judgments

Read on the net diff against the merge base `6e287974` (41 files, +124 / -65); `main` at `e9884e19` has not touched `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts` since.

- **Public surface of `@object-ui/data-objectstack`: exactly one name leaves, none enters. Right.** `package.json` publishes one entry (`exports` holds `.` only, `files` is `dist`), and `tsup.config.ts` bundles from `src/index.ts` alone, so the new module is not a reachable subpath and its unexported helper is not in the built entry. `index.ts` now re-exports `getSharedDiscovery` by name from `./sharedDiscovery` and nothing else from it.
- **`getSharedDiscovery` keeps its name, signature and behaviour. Right.** The removed block and the new module are the same text (the Map, the function, the helper); `discoveryCache` has no reader left in `index.ts`; `connect()` at `index.ts:3831` and the two outside readers (`languageSeed.ts:109`, `ConditionalAuthWrapper.tsx:55`) call it as before. `serverOriginOf` stays where it was.
- **Accept-set: unchanged. Right.** No schema, wire shape, request or stored value moves; `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct (no path under `packages/spec`).
- **The 38 test files: import lines only. Right.** The diff over those files, sorted and counted, is import statements and nothing else, apart from the two side-effect imports in `canvasDataSource-27585.test.tsx`. All ten relative paths resolve to `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/sharedDiscovery` (depths checked one by one).
- **One module instance in the cross-package tests. Right.** `ui/vitest.config.mts:538` and `ui/apps/console/vite.config.ts:640` alias `@object-ui/data-objectstack` to the package `src`, whose `index.ts` imports `./sharedDiscovery`; the relative import names the same file, so the adapter and the helper share one cache. None of the ten files calls `vi.resetModules()` or mocks the package, so the reset still reaches the cache the adapter reads.
- **No reader left behind. Right.** At the head the name appears only in the module, the comment in `index.ts`, the changeset and the 38 tests, each importing from `sharedDiscovery`. On `main` at `e9884e19` the reader set is the same 38 tests plus `index.ts` (no test added since the base), so no merge skew. Org code search: 38 hits, all in this repo; hotcrm 0.
- **`canvasDataSource-27585.test.tsx` side-effect imports. Right.** `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/formula` are declared dependencies of `@object-ui/app-shell` (`package.json:95-96`), and the same module-top `@objectstack/lint` spelling is already in 87 app-shell test files. No assertion changes.
- **Gate verdicts.** Check-runs on this head, read at 2026-11-15T05:33Z: 63 runs, 46 success, 17 skipped, 0 failed, none pending. Among the successes: Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Test UI 16/16 shards, Check Changeset, the PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, and every `Lint ·` and `Type Check ·` family. The skipped runs are the path-filtered core jobs, the opt-in harnesses, the queue-verdict jobs and `UI Published Artifacts`.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

The changeset bumps `@object-ui/data-objectstack` at `patch` with a `!` title. That is the level `AGENTS.md` gives a breaking change outside the metadata protocol ("a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition"). The body carries both declaration lines, identical to the PR body's, a BREAKING paragraph, one FROM → TO line for the one name, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`runtime-export-retired @object-ui/data-objectstack#clearSharedDiscoveryCache`). Only one package's entry changes, and only that package is bumped. The level and the declaration match what the diff publishes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` in os-dev-report 6889629117 is empty. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation "two side-effect imports beyond the import line": answered in ①; the gate that asked for them is green on this head.
- Deviation "branch not merged with `main`": answered in ①; `main` has no new reader of the name and no change to `index.ts`.
- Deviations on assignees, labels and the detached checkout are process, with no contract effect.
- Earlier notes on this card (6594905321, 6660207006, 6677640939) said the helper "needs a test-support home first". That was a scoping note, not a ruling, and amendment 6888438983 names the direct module import instead. The tree supports the amendment: the cache is module state inside `data-objectstack`, so `@object-ui/test-support` could only re-export it, and the sibling helpers already cross packages by relative source path on `main` (`resetRuntimeConfigForTesting` and `resetInflightGetsForTesting` from console tests, `__clearRecordEditableCache` from app-shell tests). Answered, not escalated.
- Out-of-scope findings (the `runner` move, 57 newly confirmed i18n keys) are follow-ups on the card and are not in this diff.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing takes away no declared capability. `clearSharedDiscoveryCache` is named in no README, docs page, skill or spec; its only readers in either repo are tests; and the card's own bullet, approved by the maintainer at filing, lists it among the nine test-only helpers to move off the public barrels. The package keeps every documented cache control (`invalidateCache`, `clearCache`, `getCacheStats`) and the documented `getSharedDiscovery`. This is the same shape as the eight siblings already landed.

Attempts to break it, and what they found:

- A second copy of the cache in tests (helper clears one Map, adapter reads another): not reachable, see the module-instance judgment in ①.
- The helper leaking back out through a subpath or the built entry: not reachable, one `exports` entry and one bundle entry.
- A production path that needed the reset (logout, origin change): none. The cache is keyed by `baseUrl`, so an origin change is a new key; a failed read deletes its own entry and is retried; no logout path in the tree called the helper before this diff. A host cannot now force a re-read of a successful discovery at the same `baseUrl` within one page load, but that was never offered as an API and nothing in the Console does it. If a host ever needs it, that is a new, named capability on the entry, not this helper.
- A source-text scanner or export ratchet pinned to the old block: the scripts suite, the type-check families and all UI test shards are green on this head.

Findings:

- **nit** — `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/sharedDiscovery.ts:33`: the moved JSDoc still reads "Test/dev helper to drop the cache (e.g. on logout or origin change)", while the module header four lines up and the changeset call it test-only, and no logout or origin-change path uses it. Moved verbatim as the amendment asked; a later edit can shorten it to "Test-only". No effect on behaviour.
- **nit** — the changeset's FROM → TO line offers "or stubs the fetch its adapter makes" as a way to get a fresh discovery read. `getSharedDiscovery` returns the cached promise before it calls the fetcher, so a stub alone does not re-read a `baseUrl` already answered in the same module instance. The first alternative (a `baseUrl` per case) is correct; `vi.resetModules()` would be the accurate second one. The affected reader is a host test with zero known instances.
- **nit** — the new module carries the Apache-2.0 one-line header, while the code came from the MIT-headed `index.ts` and the package's `LICENSE` and `package.json` say MIT. 24 files in the package's `src` already carry the same header, so this follows an existing drift rather than starting one.

No must-fix and no should-fix. The three nits are left as accepted deviations or a follow-up; none needs this head to move.
